segments.source: A ll the birds were called together.
To them was said, “Whichever one of you can fly farthest into the sky shall be chief.”
All the birds flew to a great height.
But Wren got under the thick feathers of Eagle and sat there as Eagle flew.
When all the birds became wing-tired, they flew down again; but Eagle flew still higher.
When Eagle had gone as far as he could, Wren flew still higher.
When all the birds reached the ground, Eagle alone returned, after a great while.
Eagle had too highly been thinking of himself, being sure of being made chief; and behold!
